`React.PureComponent` already decides when to render again: it compares the old and new props and state. A `shouldComponentUpdate` of your own replaces that comparison, so extending `PureComponent` no longer does anything. Keep one of the two.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
class Price extends React.PureComponent {
  shouldComponentUpdate(nextProps) {
    return nextProps.amount !== this.props.amount;
  }

  render() {
    return <span>{this.props.amount}</span>;
  }
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
class Price extends React.PureComponent {
  render() {
    return <span>{this.props.amount}</span>;
  }
}

class Total extends React.Component {
  shouldComponentUpdate(nextProps) {
    return nextProps.amount !== this.props.amount;
  }

  render() {
    return <strong>{this.props.amount}</strong>;
  }
}
```
